title: One ornament, two turns
odia:
ନାକ ଚଣା ବୋଲି ଖଣ୍ଡେ
ତାକୁ ବୋହୂ ନାଉଥାଏ ଦଣ୍ଡେ
ତାକୁ ଶାଶୁ ନାଉଥାଏ ଦଣ୍ଡେ।
literal_meaning: Just one nose ornament: the daughter-in-law wears it for a while, and the mother-in-law wears it for a while.
meaning_odia: ନାକଚଣା ଖଣ୍ଡିଏ ଅଛି; ତାକୁ ବୋହୂ କିଛି ସମୟ ପିନ୍ଧୁଛନ୍ତି, ପୁଣି ଶାଶୁ କିଛି ସମୟ ପିନ୍ଧୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ଅଳ୍ପ ସାମଗ୍ରୀକୁ ଏକାଧିକ ଲୋକ ପାଳି କରି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। ଦୁହିଁଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଝଗଡ଼ା କିମ୍ବା କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରଥା ଏଥିରେ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
explanation: The repeated lines pass the same ornament from one wearer to the other. Our editorial reading focuses on limited means: two people’s wishes are accommodated through turns with a single object. The verse leaves their feelings about the arrangement unstated.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Two colleagues have only one piece of equipment between them and arrange alternating turns. Someone recalls the single ornament worn first by one household member and then by the other.
cultural_context: The household relationship gives the repeated action two distinct participants, while ଖଣ୍ଡେ keeps the available ornament singular. Repeating ଦଣ୍ଡେ makes the alternation audible. The scene can be understood without treating it as a documented household practice.

witnesses.locator: Page27, third item beginning ନାକ ଚଣା.
witnesses.note: Rendered upload inspected17November2026; exact wording and three-line layout retained. ନାଉଥାଏ rendered wears, and ଦଣ୍ଡେ for a while without a fixed duration. Expanded interpretation is editorial.

odia_summary: ନାକଚଣା ଖଣ୍ଡିଏକୁ ଶାଶୁ ଓ ବୋହୂ ପାଳି କରି ପିନ୍ଧନ୍ତି।
english_summary: A single ornament is worn by two people in turns.
